Next steps: what in the restored W51 images still needs work¶

28 October 2026. Follows report_restoration_20261027.ipynb (the methods and checks) and saturated_pixel_kinds_20261028.ipynb (the kinds of saturated pixels).

The story. The restored images now fill 84-100% of the sky pixels that were saturated in every exposure. Two weak spots of the first version were fixed after a review: the F2100W cores, whose filled values differed between the two observations, and the F410M cores, which were empty. This notebook

  1. shows each fix on the images, before and after (sections 1-2),
  2. checks whether neighbouring pixels restored by different methods join smoothly (section 3),
  3. compares the methods on the same sky pixel, measured or restored in different exposures (section 4),
  4. shows close-ups of what still needs work, with numbers (section 5),
  5. ends with the decisions to make (section 6).
term meaning
exposure, dither, observation one image; the exposures are shifted slightly (dithers), so a sky position falls on different detector pixels. MIRI F2100W has two observations (001, 002), taken at different times
response curve MIRI: the measured relation between collected charge and recorded signal above the saturation flag; read backwards to get the brightness
core pixels already at the detector's hard ceiling in their first read; they hold no reading of their own
cross-filter fill a core pixel predicted from its brightness in the other filters (censored fit); F2100W is then scaled ("pinned") to match SOFIA's 3" image
floor the smallest value a core pixel can have: the brightness of a pixel whose first read just reached the top of the response curve. A fill below it is raised to it, so a pixel at the floor holds a lower limit
dex a factor in log10: 0.01 dex = 2.3%, 0.1 dex = 26%
METHOD the code of the method that gave a pixel its value (colours in the method maps)

from reproject import reproject_interp
from astropy.wcs import FITSFixedWarning

from mosaic_restored import wcs_of
from merge_restored import METHODS

BLUE, ORANGE, AQUA, YELLOW = '#2a78d6', '#eb6834', '#1baf7a', '#eda100'
INK, MUTED, GREY, LIGHT = '#0b0b0b', '#52514e', '#b5b4ae', '#e6e5e0'
plt.rcParams.update({'axes.spines.top': False, 'axes.spines.right': False, 'axes.grid': True, 'grid.color': LIGHT,
                     'grid.linewidth': 0.6, 'axes.edgecolor': GREY, 'axes.labelcolor': INK, 'xtick.color': MUTED,
                     'ytick.color': MUTED, 'lines.linewidth': 2, 'font.size': 11, 'axes.titlesize': 12,
                     'axes.titleweight': 'bold', 'legend.frameon': False, 'figure.dpi': 110})
P = '/orange/adamginsburg/w51/TaehwaYoo/w51_sat_recover/production'
FIN = f'{P}/final'
CAL = {'MIRI': '/orange/adamginsburg/w51/jwst/jwst_new_cal_claude_satstep/{f}/pipeline_4qpm/{n}_cal.fits',
       'NIRCam': '/orange/adamginsburg/jwst/w51/{f}/pipeline/{n}_cal.fits'}
MCOL = [LIGHT, '#cfcdc6', AQUA, BLUE, '#8fbbec', YELLOW, ORANGE, '#f6d48c', '#a3261f', '#f3b38a']   # METHOD codes 0-9
mcmap = ListedColormap(MCOL)

def restored(f, n):
    with fits.open(f'{FIN}/{f}/{n}_restored.fits') as h:
        return h['SCI'].data.astype(float), h['METHOD'].data

def floor_of(n):
    # the merge floor (merge_restored.py): median curve value of pixels whose first read reached 95% of the curve's top
    with fits.open(f'{P}/miri_ramp/restored/{n}_ramp.fits') as h:
        rs, rm, rq = h['SCI'].data, h['METHOD'].data, h['Q0'].data
    inv = np.isin(rm, [2, 3]) & np.isfinite(rq) & np.isfinite(rs)
    return np.nanmedian(rs[inv & (rq >= 0.95 * np.nanmax(rq[inv]))]), rm

def old_f2100w(n):
    # the F2100W exposure as it was before the fix: fill pinned with a SOFIA scale per group (miri_xband/filled/), floored
    sci, m = restored('F2100W', n)
    xs = fits.getdata(f'{P}/miri_xband/filled/{n}_xband_sofia.fits', 'SCI')
    floor, rm = floor_of(n)
    old = sci.copy()
    f6 = m == 6
    old[f6] = np.where((rm[f6] == 4) & (xs[f6] < floor), floor, xs[f6])
    return old, sci, m

def window(mask, half, x0=0):
    # the (2 half)^2 window with the most pixels in mask, kept on the detector
    d = ndimage.uniform_filter(mask.astype(float), 2 * half)
    d[:half], d[-half:], d[:, :x0 + half], d[:, -half:] = 0, 0, 0, 0
    cy, cx = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(d), d.shape)
    return slice(cy - half, cy + half), slice(cx - half, cx + half)

def show_img(ax, img, norm, title):
    cm = plt.get_cmap('magma').copy(); cm.set_bad(ORANGE)
    ax.imshow(img, origin='lower', cmap=cm, norm=norm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)

def show_method(ax, m, title='method'):
    ax.imshow(m, origin='lower', cmap=mcmap, vmin=-0.5, vmax=9.5, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)

def method_legend(fig, codes, **kw):
    fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=MCOL[k], ec=GREY, label=METHODS[k]) for k in codes], loc='lower center', ncol=5, fontsize=10, **kw)

hw = lambda e: (np.percentile(e, 84) - np.percentile(e, 16)) / 2

1. The F2100W fix: the same core in two observations¶

What was wrong. The cross-filter fill of a core is scaled so that its 3" average matches SOFIA times a factor. That factor used to be measured in a ring around each core, separately for each group of exposures, and it came out 0.24 dex different between observations 001 and 002. The fix: one scale for all exposures, fitted on measured pixels only, and one fit over all 16 exposures together.

The figure shows one core as seen in an exposure of observation 001 and one of observation 002 (the pair that shares the most filled core pixels), before the fix (top) and after it (bottom). The right column is the ratio of the two observations on the same sky: white is agreement, blue is observation 002 fainter.

In [2]:
import glob
names = lambda f: sorted(p.split('/')[-1].replace('_restored.fits', '') for p in glob.glob(f'{FIN}/{f}/*_restored.fits'))
def pair(A, B):
    # exposure B (old and new values, METHOD) on the pixels of exposure A, and the core pixels filled in both
    wA, wB = wcs_of(CAL['MIRI'].format(f='F2100W', n=A)), wcs_of(CAL['MIRI'].format(f='F2100W', n=B))
    oldA, newA, mA = old_f2100w(A)
    oldB, newB, mB = old_f2100w(B)
    onA = lambda img: reproject_interp((img, wB), wA, shape_out=oldA.shape, order='nearest-neighbor')[0]
    oldB, newB, mBA = onA(oldB), onA(newB), onA(mB.astype(float))
    both = (mA == 6) & (mBA == 6) & np.isfinite(oldA) & np.isfinite(oldB) & np.isfinite(newA) & np.isfinite(newB)
    return oldA, newA, oldB, newB, both

# the pair of exposures of tile 02109, one from each observation, that shares the most filled core pixels
cands = [(a, b) for a in names('F2100W') if '2001_02109' in a for b in names('F2100W') if '2002_02109' in b]
A, B = max(cands, key=lambda ab: pair(*ab)[4].sum())
oldA, newA, oldB, newB, both = pair(A, B)
print('observation 001:', A, ' observation 002:', B)
sl = window(both, 50, x0=365)
v = np.nanpercentile(newA[sl], [2, 99.8]); norm = LogNorm(v[0], v[1])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 11))
rcm = plt.get_cmap('RdBu_r').copy(); rcm.set_bad(LIGHT)
for r, (a, b, lab) in enumerate([(oldA, oldB, 'before the fix'), (newA, newB, 'after the fix')]):
    show_img(ax[r, 0], a[sl], norm, f'{lab}: observation 001')
    show_img(ax[r, 1], b[sl], norm, f'{lab}: observation 002')
    im = ax[r, 2].imshow(np.where(both, np.log10(b / a), np.nan)[sl], origin='lower', cmap=rcm, vmin=-0.3, vmax=0.3, interpolation='nearest')
    ax[r, 2].set_title(f'{lab}: log10(002 / 001)'); ax[r, 2].set_xticks([]); ax[r, 2].set_yticks([]); ax[r, 2].grid(False)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax[:, 2], fraction=0.05, label='dex (grey: not a fill pixel in both)')
plt.show()
r_old, r_new = np.log10(oldB / oldA)[both], np.log10(newB / newA)[both]
pd.DataFrame({'before the fix': [both.sum(), np.median(r_old), hw(r_old)], 'after the fix': [both.sum(), np.median(r_new), hw(r_new)]},
             index=['core pixels filled in both', 'median log10(002/001), dex', 'half-width, dex']).round(3)

Over all exposures (production/miri_xband/README.md): two exposures from different observations now agree to 0.029 dex (0.126 before), exposures overall to 0.019 dex (0.061), and the share of core pixels at the floor fell from 23% to 19%.

What the fix does not settle. The level of all F2100W cores together: tested against hidden response-curve pixels, the cores sit 0.03-0.05 dex low, about twice the uncertainty of the SOFIA scale. The close-ups also show places where the inside of a core is not brighter than its rim. On average the cores do rise inward (+0.03 to +0.06 dex above the floor at the edge, +0.34 to +0.37 dex deeper than 10 px, in the two exposures shown), but 17-22% of their pixels sit at or near the floor, the level of the brightest rim pixels.

2. The F410M fix: filling the cores from the other filters¶

What was wrong. NIRCam's F410M cores are flat already in the first read (10.7 s), so they held no value. The fix: a cross-filter fill from F405N, F335M, F360M or F480M, which still have a value from their first read there; tested on first-read pixels of known value to +0.02-0.03 dex. Where F360M is saturated too, the fill uses F560W and F210M; that set failed its test (-0.04 dex, scatter 0.2 dex) and is marked low confidence (light orange).

The figure shows the brightest F410M core in one exposure: before the fix (orange: empty), after it, and the method of each pixel.

In [4]:

fill = np.isin(m, [6, 9])
sl = window(fill, 60)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 6.4))
show_img(ax[0], np.where(fill, np.nan, sci)[sl], norm, 'F410M before the fix (orange: empty)')

Reading the figure.

  • The large empty core is now filled. Most of its inside comes from the low-confidence set (light orange), its outer part from the accepted set (orange).
  • Still empty (dark red): the centre of the brightest core, where every input filter is saturated, and a thin ring between the fill and the pipeline values. The ring holds pixels next to a ceiling pixel, whose first read contains charge spilled from it, and pixels the pipeline marked "do not use" although they kept good reads (saturated_pixel_kinds_20261028.ipynb, section 6).
  • Over all exposures the empty F410M sky pixels went from 6,556 to 1,454.

3. Do the filled cores join their neighbours?¶

A core pixel was at the ceiling in its first read and its neighbours outside the core were not, so it collected more light: it should be at least as bright as they are. The figure compares each filled pixel at a core edge with the mean of its neighbours within 2 px that come from another method (the response curve in F2100W; the pipeline value and the first read in F410M). Zero is an exact match; a small positive value is what a smooth rise into the core gives.

In [5]:
def edge_steps(sci, m, inner, outer, r=2):
    # log10(inner pixel / mean of its outer-method neighbours within r px), for inner pixels that have such neighbours
    nb = np.isin(m, outer) & np.isfinite(sci)
    k = 2 * r + 1
    num = ndimage.uniform_filter(np.where(nb, sci, 0), k); den = ndimage.uniform_filter(nb.astype(float), k)
    sel = np.isin(m, inner) & np.isfinite(sci) & (den > 0)
    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
        e = np.log10(sci[sel] / (num[sel] / den[sel]))
    return e[np.isfinite(e)]   # drops the few non-positive values

e_old, e_new = [], []
for n in names('F2100W'):
    old, new, m = old_f2100w(n)
    e_old.append(edge_steps(old, m, [6], [3, 4])); e_new.append(edge_steps(new, m, [6], [3, 4]))
e_old, e_new = np.concatenate(e_old), np.concatenate(e_new)
e6, e9 = [], []
for n in names('F410M'):
    s, mm = restored('F410M', n)
    e6.append(edge_steps(s, mm, [6], [0, 2])); e9.append(edge_steps(s, mm, [9], [0, 2]))
e6, e9 = np.concatenate(e6), np.concatenate(e9)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 4.8))
bins = np.linspace(-0.6, 1.3, 140)
ax[0].hist(e_old, bins, color=GREY, label=f'before the fix: median {np.median(e_old):+.3f} dex')
ax[0].hist(e_new, bins, histtype='step', lw=2.2, color=BLUE, label=f'after the fix: median {np.median(e_new):+.3f} dex')
ax[0].set_title('F2100W: core fill against the response curve next to it')
ax[1].hist(e6, bins, color=ORANGE, alpha=0.8, label=f'cross-filter fill: median {np.median(e6):+.3f} dex ({len(e6):,})')
ax[1].hist(e9, bins, histtype='step', lw=2.2, color='#c46a3a', label=f'low confidence: median {np.median(e9):+.3f} dex ({len(e9):,})')
ax[1].set_title('F410M: core fill against pipeline and first-read pixels next to it')
for a in ax:
    a.axvline(0, color=INK, lw=1); a.legend(fontsize=9.5, loc='upper right'); a.set_ylim(0, a.get_ylim()[1] * 1.3)
    a.set_xlabel('log10(fill pixel / mean of its neighbours within 2 px), dex')
ax[0].set_ylabel('pixel-exposures')
plt.tight_layout()
pd.DataFrame({k: [len(e), np.median(e), np.percentile(e, 16), np.percentile(e, 84), np.mean(e < 0)] for k, e in

             index=['n', 'median', 'p16', 'p84', 'share fainter than neighbours']).round(3)

Reading the figure.

  • F2100W: the edges are continuous before and after the fix (median +0.027 dex). The fix tightened the low side (16th percentile -0.10 → -0.035 dex), and 24% of the edge pixels are fainter than their neighbours (25% before). A narrow peak at zero holds the pixels raised to the floor.
  • F410M accepted fill: every edge pixel is brighter than its neighbours, by a median of 0.19 dex (55%). Part of this is real: the filled pixels must be above the ceiling (about 4,150 MJy/sr), the neighbours below it, and the thin unrestored ring sits between them. But the step is larger than the 0.04 dex accuracy of the fill would suggest.
  • F410M low-confidence fill: a median step of +0.62 dex (a factor of 4). These pixels come out much brighter than the pixels around them, which points to the low-confidence set overestimating the brightest cores.

4. The same sky pixel valued by different methods¶

Because of the dithers, one sky pixel can be measured in one exposure and restored in another, or restored by two different methods. For every pair of methods the table compares the two values on the sky pixels that have both: the median of log10(first / second) and its spread (half the 16-84% range), with the number of sky pixels in brackets. A good pair has a median near 0 and a small spread. A pair involving "unsaturated or pipeline value" is biased by selection: where one exposure measured a pixel and another saturated, the saturated one usually saw the brighter side of a steep profile.

In [6]:
FILTERS = ['F182M', 'F410M', 'F560W', 'F770W', 'F1000W', 'F1280W', 'F2100W']
c = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f'{FIN}/kinds/consistency_{f}.csv').assign(filter=f) for f in FILTERS])
c = c[(c.n >= 50) & np.isfinite(c.halfwidth_dex)]
c['pair'] = c.method_i + '  vs  ' + c.method_j
pairs = c.groupby('pair').n.sum().sort_values(ascending=False).index
med = c.pivot(index='pair', columns='filter', values='median_dex').reindex(index=pairs, columns=FILTERS)
hwd = c.pivot(index='pair', columns='filter', values='halfwidth_dex').reindex(index=pairs, columns=FILTERS)
nn = c.pivot(index='pair', columns='filter', values='n').reindex(index=pairs, columns=FILTERS)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 0.55 * len(pairs) + 2))
dcm = plt.get_cmap('RdBu_r').copy(); dcm.set_bad('white')

for i in range(med.shape[0]):

            ax.text(j, i, f'{med.values[i, j]:+.2f} ± {hwd.values[i, j]:.2f}\n({int(nn.values[i, j]):,})', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=8.5,
                    color='white' if abs(med.values[i, j]) > 0.2 else INK)

Reading the figure. Blue: the first method gives less than the second; red: more.

  • The MIRI ramp methods agree. Level-1 corrected against the response curve: -0.004 to -0.023 dex in F770W-F2100W, spread 0.03-0.04 dex. Pipeline against response curve: within 0.01 dex in F770W-F1280W. The less reliable response curve (code 4) runs 0.03-0.06 dex above the regular curve in every MIRI filter; part of this may be the same selection effect as for the pipeline pairs.
  • F2100W after the fix: the response curve and the fill agree to +0.02 dex (34,192 sky pixels), the less reliable curve and the fill to -0.01 dex. The fill joins the ramp methods.
  • F770W, F1000W, F1280W: the response curve comes out 0.11-0.13 dex (29-34%) above the fill on the same sky. The fill runs low in these filters, which matches the large share of core pixels at the floor (section 5.1). The less reliable curve and the fill agree (-0.01 dex) because both are mostly at the floor there.
  • F410M: the accepted fill and the low-confidence fill differ by -0.09 ± 0.11 dex (382 sky pixels): the low-confidence fill is 23% brighter where both exist. First read against the accepted fill: -0.05 ± 0.14 dex (63). The trusted star model and the low-confidence one differ by -0.06 dex (458).
  • F182M: first read against star model -0.10 ± 0.26 dex (98), star model against low-confidence star model -0.08 ± 0.33 dex (54). The spreads are large: few sky pixels, on steep star profiles.
  • MIRI low-confidence star model: where it overlaps the response curve or the fill (77-222 sky pixels in F560W, F1280W, F2100W) it is 1.4-1.9 dex lower, a factor of 25-80. These "stars" sit in saturated extended emission, and the star fit misses that emission. These pixels should not keep the star-model value.

5. What still needs work, with close-ups¶

Each item below shows the current version of the restored images.

5.1 MIRI cores at the floor (lower limits)¶

The maps colour each core pixel by whether its fill is above the floor (orange) or was raised to it (dark red: a lower limit); empty pixels are black. Over all exposures the share at the floor is 97% in F770W, 96% in F1000W, 56% in F1280W and 19% in F2100W.

In [7]:
def floor_map(f, n):
    # 0 other, 1 response curve, 2 fill above the floor, 3 fill at the floor (a lower limit), 4 empty
    sci, m = restored(f, n)
    floor, rm = floor_of(n)
    k = np.zeros(m.shape, int)
    core = (m == 6) & (rm == 4)   # filled core pixels (not the coronagraph panes)
    k[np.isin(m, [3, 4])] = 1
    k[core] = 2
    k[core & (np.abs(sci / floor - 1) < 1e-3)] = 3
    k[np.isnan(sci)] = 4
    return sci, k

FCOL = ListedColormap([LIGHT, BLUE, ORANGE, '#a3261f', '#2b2a27'])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 19))
for row, f in zip(ax, ['F770W', 'F1280W', 'F2100W']):
    n = max(names(f), key=lambda n: (restored(f, n)[1] == 6).sum())   # the exposure with the most filled core pixels
    sci, k = floor_map(f, n)
    sl = window(np.isin(k, [2, 3]), 60, x0=365)
    v = np.nanpercentile(sci[sl], [2, 99.9])
    show_img(row[0], sci[sl], LogNorm(v[0], v[1]), f'{f}: restored image')
    row[1].imshow(k[sl], origin='lower', cmap=FCOL, vmin=-0.5, vmax=4.5, interpolation='nearest')
    kk = k[sl]
    row[1].set_title(f'{f}: {np.mean(kk[(kk == 2) | (kk == 3)] == 3):.0%} of the filled core pixels here at the floor'); row[1].set_xticks([]); row[1].set_yticks([]); row[1].grid(False)
fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=c, ec=GREY, label=l) for c, l in zip([LIGHT, BLUE, ORANGE, '#a3261f', '#2b2a27'],
           ['other', 'response curve', 'cross-filter fill, above the floor', 'cross-filter fill at the floor: a lower limit', 'empty'])],
           loc='lower center', ncol=3, fontsize=10, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))
plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.02, 1, 1))

Reading the figure.

  • F770W and F1000W: nearly the whole core sits at the floor, so it shows as a flat plateau in the image. The fill model predicts less than a ceiling pixel must have: it was trained only on pixels fainter than the cores and censored at a level well below the ceiling. The F2100W fix (training on the response-curve values, censoring at the curve's top, one fit over all exposures) has not been applied to these filters yet.
  • F1280W: the floor pixels form a band around the core, where the fill falls just short of the floor.
  • F2100W: few pixels at the floor after the fix.
  • The black disk in every filter is the brightest compact core: all the input filters are saturated there too, so no fill exists. These pixels stay empty in every exposure and make up most of the 200-600 empty sky pixels per MIRI filter.

5.2 NIRCam stars from the low-confidence star model¶

The star model fits the known star shape to a star's unsaturated wings. Where the fit itself is uncertain, its values are kept but marked low confidence (light yellow). The close-up shows the F182M star with the most low-confidence pixels among regions that have wings.

Cosmic-ray snowballs. A few low-confidence "stars" have no wings at all: the pixels 2-3 px outside them are more than 100 times fainter than the region. One example is jw06151001001_03105_00005_nrca4, at RA 290.91762, Dec 14.52725. It has 56 pixels filled with up to 80,900 MJy/sr, while the 7 other exposures of that spot read 2.5-2.9 MJy/sr. These are cosmic-ray snowballs, large charge splashes flagged as saturated, which the star model treated as stars: 10 of the 343 low-confidence regions in F182M (243 pixels) and 4 of the 2,671 in F410M (116 pixels). They explain the large spread of "unsaturated or pipeline value vs star model, low confidence" in F182M (-1.11 ± 2.07 dex, section 4).

In [8]:
best = None
for n in names('F182M'):
    s, mm = restored('F182M', n)
    lab, nl = ndimage.label(np.isin(mm, [5, 7]))
    if nl:
        for i, sl in enumerate(ndimage.find_objects(lab), 1):
            sl = tuple(slice(max(a.start - 4, 0), a.stop + 4) for a in sl)
            reg = lab[sl] == i
            cnt = (mm[sl][reg] == 7).sum()
            if best is not None and cnt <= best[0]:
                continue
            ring = ndimage.binary_dilation(reg, iterations=3) & ~ndimage.binary_dilation(reg, iterations=1)
            if np.nanmax(s[sl][ring]) < np.nanmedian(s[sl][reg]) / 100:   # no wings: a cosmic-ray snowball, shown in the text below
                continue
            cy, cx = ndimage.center_of_mass(reg)
            best = (cnt, n, (cy + sl[0].start, cx + sl[1].start))
_, n, (cy, cx) = best
s, mm = restored('F182M', n)
cy, cx, h = int(cy), int(cx), 25
sl = (slice(cy - h, cy + h), slice(cx - h, cx + h))
v = np.nanpercentile(s[sl], [2, 99.9])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 6.2))
show_img(ax[0], s[sl], LogNorm(v[0], v[1]), 'F182M: restored star')
show_method(ax[1], mm[sl])
method_legend(fig, sorted(set(np.unique(mm[sl]).astype(int))), bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.05))
plt.tight_layout()

Reading the figure. The centre of this star comes from the low-confidence model (light yellow), the rest of the saturated area from the trusted star model. Summed over the star, low-confidence stars come out too bright against exposures that measured them: by 0.09 dex (23%) in F182M (56 star-exposures) and 0.03 dex (7%) in F410M (1,270). The trusted star model agrees to +0.02 dex (F182M) and +0.006 dex (F410M).

6. Decisions to make¶

Ordered by how many sky pixels each item changes and how large the error is. The first column is the recommendation.

1 F770W, F1000W, F1280W cores the fill runs 0.11-0.13 dex below the response curve; 56-97% of the filled core pixels sit at the floor (a lower limit) (a) repeat the F2100W fix: one fit over all exposures, trained on the response-curve values, censored at the curve's top; (b) keep as lower limits (a), first; the code exists and took about an hour for F2100W
2 MIRI low-confidence star model inside extended emission 1.4-1.9 dex below the response curve and the fill on the same sky (F560W, F1280W, F2100W) (a) use the response curve or the fill there instead; (b) drop the value (empty) (a); a small change in the merge order

7 cosmic-ray snowballs filled as stars 14 regions (359 pixels) in F182M and F410M get star-model values up to 80,900 MJy/sr where the other exposures read about 3 MJy/sr (a) drop star-model values in regions without wings (2-3 px ring more than 100 times fainter); (b) leave them (a); a one-line rule in the merge

Items 1 and 2 change the most pixels for the least work. After them, the consistency table of section 4 can be rerun with py/method_consistency.py to check that the response curve and the fill agree in every MIRI filter, as they now do in F2100W.
